messages:
maria: Quick question — before I open an RFC: are we comfortable making policy adapters able to run asynchronously (i.e. return a promise/future) and the policy engine to await them up to an evaluation budget?

sam: I think async adapters are fine, but the tricky part is enforcing a hard budget and deterministic tie-breaks if some adapters time out.

kai: +1 on async. Two concerns: (1) policy side-effects (if an adapter hits external service) — we need a sandbox contract, and (2) how this interacts with hot-reload of policies (race conditions).

jen: for (1) we should forbid adapters from doing side-effects in the hot path. They can return hints but not mutate routing state. If someone needs side-effects they should do them in an async enrichment step that is not part of the decision path.

infra-bot: deploybot: new image pushed to staging for policy-sandbox v0.3 :rocket:

sam: Proposed model: each policy adapter returns {score_delta, deterministic_key?} and optionally an explanation blob. The engine keeps a per-request evaluation_budget_ms (default 35ms). Adapters that don't respond in time are treated as neutral (score_delta = 0) and flagged in telemetry.

maria: That seems reasonable. How do we ensure deterministic results when adapters race and sometimes return after the budget? We can't have nondeterministic routing between retries.

kai: Add two rules: (A) policy ordering is explicit and stable (no implicit alphabetical ordering), and (B) if an adapter times out we record a deterministic penalty instead of 'neutral' so tie-breakers are stable. E.g., timeout_penalty = -0.001 * adapter_order_index.

sam: I like deterministic penalties but worried about surprising behavior. Maybe make it opt-in per-tenant via config, default = neutral. But we must guarantee that replay (same seed) yields same decisions. So we also need to record the evaluation snapshot in request trace: which adapters timed out, evaluation_budget, seed/tiebreaker used.

jen: another approach: keep all adapters pure and side-effect-free, but have the engine evaluate them in two phases: synchronous quick-path (fast adapters) and async enrichment. Quick-path must hit the SLO (e.g., 15ms) and decide. Async enrichment can update cached routes for next requests. This reduces variance.

maria: That split feels future-proof. For the near term though, do we agree on: async adapters allowed; engine enforces per-adapter and total budget; timeouts treated as recorded neutral by default but with optional deterministic_penalty flag; audit fields recorded in traces?

kai: yep. Also add a liveness guard: if >50% of adapters time out for a tenant for 5min window, fall back to simpler policy variant (e.g., single-pass cost-only) and raise an alert.

sam: I'll draft an RFC w/ proto API sketch and how to surface metrics: adapter_latency_ms, adapter_timeouts, adapter_effective_score_delta, policy_decision_seed. Also include backwards-compat notes for existing adapters.

maria: thanks — ping me when draft is ready. Also add a little test harness that can simulate adapter jitter and hot-reload races.

jen: fwiw i can contribute the harness (will use existing policy-sim).

infra-bot: incidentbot: note: added metric policy_adapter_timeout_count to staging metrics.

maria: cool. moving to RFC phase. :+1:
